sources.title: FCC Approves 49.5% Foreign Ownership of Paramount-Warner Bros.

discussion.body: The 25% threshold is the whole story here. A company can be almost half foreign-owned as long as regulators agree it is still controlled from home.
Approval of a petition is not the same as clearance of the merger. This is one gate opening, not the finish line.

items.title: FCC Lets Nearly Half of Paramount Be Foreign-Owned After Warner Deal
items.body:
The Federal Communications Commission on Thursday approved Paramount's petition to let 49.5% of its equity sit with foreign entities once its Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition closes. The reason this needs a vote at all: Paramount owns 28 TV stations, and foreign ownership above 25% requires FCC approval.

Variety reports the acquisition is backed by three Gulf parties. What the approval does not settle, at least in the excerpt available, is who exercises control rather than simply holding equity — and the FCC's sign-off is a regulatory gate, not the closing of the deal itself.

sources.title: UN experts say grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran strikes

discussion.body: Expert-panel findings carry moral and political weight, but they are not convictions. The wording "grounds to believe" signals exactly that gap.
Which makes the silence notable: per the report, the US has not acknowledged the strikes the finding is built around.

items.title: UN Experts Say Grounds Exist to Believe US Committed War Crimes in Iran Strikes
items.body:
A group of UN experts says there are grounds to believe the United States committed war crimes in strikes on Iran, according to the BBC. The reported targets include a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd, struck in February. The BBC notes the US has not acknowledged carrying out those strikes.

"Grounds to believe" is the language of an expert finding, not a court verdict — an important distinction when the underlying attribution is itself in dispute.

sources.title: San Sebastián 2026: ’Les Mis,’ Los Javis, Brad Pitt, Penélope Cruz and Much More

items.title: San Sebastián Opens With Brad Pitt Back in the Basque Country
items.body:
The San Sebastián Film Festival runs Sept. 18–26, and Variety's preview flags Brad Pitt's return — his first time back since "Inglourious Basterds" — with "Heart of the Beast." Penélope Cruz is described as the festival's busiest star, with Naomi Watts also among the names expected.

For anyone tracking awards-season positioning rather than red carpets, the useful signal is a festival calendar that now mixes A-list premieres with the usual Basque-country backdrop.

sources.title: Early Bowie music available to stream for first time

items.title: Early Bowie Recordings Reach Streaming for the First Time
items.body:
Previously unheard material from the very start of David Bowie's career has been released for the first time, the BBC reports — and is now available to stream, where it had not been before.

The interesting part is not novelty for its own sake but the archive problem: early sessions often sit in limbo for decades over rights, tape condition, and who actually owns the master. When they surface, what listeners get is the sound of an artist before the persona hardened into place.
